subsystems.name: Memory cell array
subsystems.role: stores each bit as a tiny electric charge in a capacitor, gated by a transistor.

subsystems.name: Address decoding and command logic
subsystems.role: turns requests from the memory controller into precise row and column selections.

subsystems.name: Sense amplifiers and I/O
subsystems.role: detects the minuscule charge on each cell and drives the data out at high speed.

subsystems.name: Refresh circuitry
subsystems.role: rewrites each cell periodically, because the capacitor charge leaks away.

subsystems.name: High-speed interface
subsystems.role: moves data between the memory and the processor or memory controller.

subsystems.name: Packaging and module
subsystems.role: protects the die and connects it to the motherboard.

buildSteps.title: Grow and slice silicon
buildSteps.detail: A pure silicon crystal is pulled from a melt, then sliced and polished into mirror-smooth wafers.

buildSteps.title: Pattern the transistors
buildSteps.detail: Photolithography, etching and deposition define billions of tiny transistors across the wafer, one per memory cell.

buildSteps.title: Form the capacitors
buildSteps.detail: Each cell gets a capacitor — either a deep trench etched into the silicon or a tall stack built above it — using high-k dielectrics to store enough charge in a very small volume.

buildSteps.title: Build the wiring
buildSteps.detail: Many layers of copper wiring are deposited and patterned to connect word lines, bit lines and control circuits.

buildSteps.title: Probe the wafer
buildSteps.detail: Test needles touch each die to check for defects and measure speed before the wafer is cut.

buildSteps.title: Dice and package
buildSteps.detail: The wafer is cut into individual dies, which are encapsulated in protective chip packages with fine metal connections.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the module
buildSteps.detail: Multiple memory chips are soldered onto a small circuit board, a serial presence detect chip is added, and a heat spreader may be attached.

buildSteps.title: Final test and binning
buildSteps.detail: Each module is tested for capacity, speed and reliability, then sorted into performance grades.

prerequisites.why: printing the smallest features of each cell requires deep-ultraviolet or extreme-ultraviolet light.

prerequisites.tech: High-k dielectrics and atomic layer deposition
prerequisites.why: capacitors must store enough charge in a volume of a few tens of nanometres without leaking.
the processor and memory must agree on signalling, timing and voltage to move data reliably.
any impurity or crystal defect can ruin millions of cells.
as cells shrink, soft errors and weak bits must be detected and corrected in use.

pathway.milestone: DDR5 and LPDDR5 modules, plus high-bandwidth memory stacked beside processors
pathway.unlocks: fast, high-capacity main memory for computers, phones and servers.

pathway.milestone: further DRAM generations and 3D-stacked memory with more layers
pathway.unlocks: higher bandwidth and capacity without a proportional increase in cost or power.

pathway.milestone: memory expansion over high-speed interconnects such as CXL
pathway.unlocks: pooled and shared memory across servers, easing capacity limits.

pathway.milestone: computing inside or very near the memory array
pathway.unlocks: less data movement, which is the main energy cost in modern computing.
